audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that this matchup never names a single Nautilus ability, and it does not: Staggering Blow, Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath, Riptide and Depth Charge are all absent from both layers, which are written entirely as 'his Q hook', 'his passive root' and 'his E AoE'.
audit.why: Difficulty in this lane is one number — Dredge Line at 14/13/12/11/10. It is his only engage, and everything Malphite does pre-4 is scheduled around it. Without the name and the cooldown the difficulty reads as a vague 'respect the hook' rather than a fourteen-second clock the player can count. At 53.22% over 4117 games this is a favoured lane and the reason is that his engage is long and telegraphed while Malphite's answer is a flat 7s.
audit.corrected: Dredge Line (Q), 14/13/12/11/10, is his only engage — the lane is the window after he throws it.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.win reads Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Skill, Skill, Malphite, Malphite — it gives Malphite levels 2 and 3 while content.early says 'pre-4 you have no trade pattern' and whys[0] says the same.
audit.why: Both cannot be true. The packet levelChart for this pairing is Nautilus, Skill, Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, which matches the prose exactly: he owns level 1 with the hook-plus-root, the middle levels are a coinflip on whether Dredge Line lands, and Malphite owns everything from 4 onward once Thunderclap and Ground Slam are up. I could not submit this as edits — the cells are one-word enums and the ±10% band rejects 'Skill' becoming 'Malphite'.
audit.corrected: win and phases sides should read: Nautilus, Skill, Skill, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite, Malphite.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer compares the two ultimates, and Depth Charge is never named.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force has 1000 range, Depth Charge 825. The existing text asserts 'your R outranges his' without the numbers, which makes it an opinion; with them it is a rule the player can position by. Depth Charge also chases a single opponent, so his ultimate answers one target while yours arrives on a group — that asymmetry is the reason the 6 spike belongs to Malphite here.
audit.corrected: Unstoppable Force reaches 1000 to Depth Charge's 825 — you engage first and he can only answer one target.

audit.whatIsWrong: Titan's Wrath is never mentioned, so the page never says why Ground Slam is the right button against him.
audit.why: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield whose damage-over-time is applied by his attacks — 'his Attacks deal damage over time to his target and surrounding enemies'. Ground Slam reduces attack speed on a flat 7s. So Malphite's E does not merely reduce his auto damage, it reduces the rate at which he applies the W effect, and it comes back nearly twice as often as the shield. That is the mechanical reason a Nautilus all-in bounces off a level 4-5 Malphite.
audit.corrected: Titan's Wrath is a flat 12s shield that damages through his autos — Ground Slam's flat 7s attack-speed cut slows the whole package.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both kits carry displacement and the page never frames the exchange.
audit.why: Dredge Line pulls, Depth Charge knocks up, Staggering Blow roots, and Unstoppable Force knocks up. The _missing-interactions entry for the Nautilus side records this as a knockup-enabler: whoever lands displacement first owns the trade. That is the honest framing. I deliberately did NOT write the companion claim in that file — that Dredge Line 'shuts off' Unstoppable Force — because nothing in either Riot description supports a hook cancelling an in-flight unstoppable dash, and the kits' needsResearch is empty by design.
audit.corrected: Whoever displaces first owns the trade: his anchor and root against your knock-up.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns said 'Nautilus Dredge Line: matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it' with no number, then two generic placeholder lines.
audit.why: The whole lane is a cooldown-window lane and none of the three windows were written down: Dredge Line 14/13/12/11/10, Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5, Titan's Wrath flat 12s. Riptide being on roughly the same clock as Ground Slam is why the level 4-5 trades come out even before armour, and the hook's fourteen seconds are why they come out ahead after it.
audit.corrected: Dredge Line 14/13/12/11/10; Riptide 7/6.5/6/5.5/5; Titan's Wrath flat 12s; your Ground Slam flat 7s.

audit.why: 53.22% over 4117 games — the largest sample in this slice and comfortably favoured, which supports the existing FAVOURED-leaning framing even though the chart cells need correcting.

edits.before: Naut's whole early game is the Q hook into his passive root — pre-4 you have no trade pattern, just Granite Shield, so the one thing to respect is getting hooked and chain-rooted before W armor and E exist. Sidestep the hook (it is a slow skillshot) and last-hit at range with Q-Seismic Shard; don't walk into minions where his E AoE and passive proc on you for free. Eat a little poke, give up the very early levels, and wait — his root means nothing once you can armor up.
edits.after: Naut's whole early game is Dredge Line (Q) into Staggering Blow, the root on his first attack — pre-4 you have no trade pattern, just Granite Shield, so the one thing to respect is getting hooked and chain-rooted before Thunderclap and Ground Slam exist. Sidestep the anchor and last-hit at range with Seismic Shard; don't sit in minions where Riptide and his passive proc for free. Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 — that is your window.

edits.before: This is where the lane flips to you. W-Thunderclap gives you bonus armor and AoE splash autos, and E-Ground Slam slows his attack speed — both scale off your armor, so a mostly-AD/auto-and-passive champion like Naut just bounces off you. Trade after he whiffs or spends his Q hook: W on, autos into him, E to gut his attack speed and passive-root damage. At 6 your R outranges his single-target ult — you knock up first and he can only answer one target.
edits.after: This is where the lane flips to you. Thunderclap gives you bonus armour and splash autos, and Ground Slam is a flat 7s attack-speed cut — Titan's Wrath (W) is a 12s shield whose damage rides his autos, so slowing them turns his all-in off. Trade after he spends Dredge Line: W on, autos in, E to gut his attack speed. At 6 Unstoppable Force reaches 1000 units to Depth Charge's 825, so you engage first and he answers one target.

notes: The flagged defect was real and total: five Nautilus abilities, none of them named anywhere in the matchup. Everything is now keyed to Dredge Line's 14s at rank 1, which is the only clock that matters pre-6. Two things I refused to assert. First, the _missing-interactions file claims Dredge Line 'shuts off' Unstoppable Force; no Riot description in either kit supports a hook cancelling an unstoppable dash mid-flight, so the page says only that whoever displaces first wins the trade. Second, Malphite's kit flags grounding on Seismic Shard and Ground Slam, which Riot's descriptions do not support — no dash-denial claim was written anywhere.
